NKE.rationale: Nike is in a severe fundamental deterioration with no credible near-term re-rating catalyst. Q3 FY2026 (Feb 2026) showed EPS of $0.35, down 35% YoY from $0.54, with operating income collapsing to $650M from $844M. Revenue was essentially flat at $11.28B while operating cash flow plunged 76% YoY to $430M. Gross margin compressed to 40.2% (down 130 bps) driven by a ~$1.5B annualized tariff headwind and inventory clearance. The turnaround under CEO Elliott Hill is showing early wholesale recovery signs (North America +3%, wholesale +5% in Q3), but this is overwhelmed by: (1) Greater China guided to decline ~20% in Q4, (2) persistent margin erosion from tariffs on Vietnam/Indonesia-sourced footwear (79% of production), (3) aggressive competitive share loss to On (+40%), Hoka (+24%), and New Balance (+19%), and (4) a P/E of ~30x on rapidly declining earnings that prices in recovery that is far from assured. The stock has fallen from $80 to $45 over the past year, yet the valuation remains expensive for a company with flat revenue, declining margins, and a multi-year turnaround ahead. RBC downgraded to $50 target citing delayed turnaround benefits not materializing until 2027. News sentiment is deeply negative (mean -0.45 over 90 days). The June 30 earnings report is a binary event with downside risk if China and margins disappoint further. All three pillars align negatively: deteriorating fundamentals, expensive valuation vs. declining earnings power, and a near-term catalyst (earnings) that carries more downside than upside risk given the trajectory.
